info.name: E-commerce - Requirement 1 & 2
info.description:
Run the whole collection in order with the Collection Runner.

Needs `docker compose up -d` and the seeded databases (admin@system.com / user@system.com, password `password123`). Stock lives only in the Warehouse service: there is no stock field on products and no stock endpoint in Laravel. Orders use seeded products that the Warehouse seed stocks (product 15 has 60 units, product 13 has 1, product 16 is not stocked). Every stock check is relative to the live quantity read first, so the collection can run repeatedly. To change stock, use the Warehouse CLI: `docker compose exec warehouse python -m app.cli set-stock <product_id> <quantity>`.

item.name: Stock unchanged after the second cancel
Race condition (last units)
item.description:
Many orders for the same product at the same moment. Run "0. Setup" first.

Reads the live stock S of race_product_id (product 13 starts with 1 unit), sends race_requests orders of 1 unit in parallel, and checks that exactly min(S, race_requests) succeed, the rest get 409, and the stock never goes below 0. Then it cancels those orders, which releases their reservations, so the stock is back to S.

php artisan serve handles requests one at a time unless PHP_CLI_SERVER_WORKERS is above 1, so this shows correctness, not true parallelism. The real concurrent test is tests/Integration (20 separate PHP processes).

item.name: Manual - Warehouse stopped (run on its own)
item.description:
Run these two requests by hand, not in the Collection Runner.

1. `docker compose stop warehouse`
2. Send the requests below.
3. `docker compose start warehouse`

Product pages stay up with stock_status `unavailable`; an order is refused with 503 and nothing is saved. To see a 504 (timeout) instead, use `docker compose pause warehouse` / `docker compose unpause warehouse`.

item.name: Requirement 3 - Cache, ETag and comparison
item.description:
Catalog reads (v1 and v2 products, categories) are cached in Redis; live stock never is.

Every catalog response has `X-Cache` (HIT, MISS, BYPASS, SKIP, OFF) and `Server-Timing` (`catalog` = time to get the catalog data from Redis or MySQL, `stock` = live GetStock call). `X-Cache-Bypass: 1` skips the cache for one request (allowed outside production), so the same request can be timed both ways in one run.

Before/after with the global switch: set `PRODUCT_CACHE_ENABLED=false` for the app in docker-compose.yml, `docker compose up -d app`, run this folder (X-Cache shows OFF), then set it back to true and run it again.

`cache_rounds` (default 20) sets how many requests per endpoint and mode the comparison sends.

The comparison sends about 300 requests, above the normal limit of 60 requests per minute per user, so run it with `API_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=100000 docker compose up -d app` and restore the default afterwards with `docker compose up -d app`.

item.name: Compare uncached vs cached (same data, same requests)

request.description: Sends cache_rounds requests per endpoint and mode, then reports p50/p95/p99 response times and the average catalog lookup time (MySQL vs Redis) from Server-Timing. The figures are the test names and are also logged to the console.

exec: // Same data, same requests: each endpoint is called ROUNDS times with the cache
// bypassed (X-Cache-Bypass: 1 -> MySQL) and ROUNDS times through the cache
// (Redis), alternating so both see the same conditions. Nothing here is a fixed
// number: every figure comes from these responses.
jobs.push({ name, path, mode: "cached", warmup: true }); // fill the cache first
pm.sendRequest({ url: base + job.path, method: "GET", header: header }, (err, res) => {
const v = values.filter(x => x !== null).sort((a, b) => a - b);
const avg = values => { const v = values.filter(x => x !== null); return v.length ? v.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / v.length : null; };
pm.test("Every request answered 200" + (bad.includes(429) ? " (429 = API rate limit: start the app with API_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=100000 for this comparison)" : ""), () => pm.expect(bad).to.eql([]));
const un = samples.filter(s => s.name === name && s.mode === "uncached");
const ca = samples.filter(s => s.name === name && s.mode === "cached");
pm.test(name + ": uncached requests really skipped the cache (X-Cache " + (cacheOff ? "OFF" : "BYPASS") + ")",
pm.test(name + ": cached requests were served from Redis (X-Cache HIT)", () => pm.expect(ca.every(s => s.xcache === "HIT")).to.eql(true));
uncached_p50_ms: f(pct(un.map(s => s.ms), 50)), uncached_p95_ms: f(pct(un.map(s => s.ms), 95)), uncached_p99_ms: f(pct(un.map(s => s.ms), 99)),
cached_p50_ms: f(pct(ca.map(s => s.ms), 50)), cached_p95_ms: f(pct(ca.map(s => s.ms), 95)), cached_p99_ms: f(pct(ca.map(s => s.ms), 99)),
catalog_uncached_avg_ms: f(avg(un.map(s => s.catalogMs))), catalog_cached_avg_ms: f(avg(ca.map(s => s.catalogMs))),
// The measured numbers are shown as test names, so they appear in the runner.
row.cache = cacheOff ? "OFF (PRODUCT_CACHE_ENABLED=false): both columns read MySQL" : "ON: bypass = MySQL, normal = Redis";
const second = cacheOff ? "second set (MySQL, cache off) " : "cached (Redis) ";
pm.test(name + " | total p50/p95: uncached (MySQL) " + row.uncached_p50_ms + "/" + row.uncached_p95_ms + " ms, " + second
+ row.cached_p50_ms + "/" + row.cached_p95_ms + " ms | catalog lookup avg: " + row.catalog_uncached_avg_ms
